new_statements.rule_in_words: Main stress on the first syllable of the word, with secondary stresses on alternating syllables thereafter (Goedemans' classification, inferred from the pre-syllable stress marks in Berndt & Vogelsang's 1941 wordlist, which itself makes no statement).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Category I implies secondary stress on alternate syllables after the initial; Goedemans notes final-syllable secondary stress is not coded. The 1941 transcriptions show second stress marks mainly on second members of compounds/reduplications (e.g. ['mana'tandra], 'pildri'pildri-type forms).
new_statements.exceptions: None flagged by Goedemans (no E/C/M/quantity-sensitive code on the entry). In the primary wordlist a minority of forms carry a non-initial mark only (e.g. [vad'napa] 'circumcision', [gundi'itji] 'it', [nena'idla] 'own').
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms (single-word elicitation from one elderly rememberer, 1940); no phrase-level information. Classification is second-hand: the primary source is a stress-marked vocabulary without any prose rule.
new_statements.identity_note: All Ngadjuri data trace to one rememberer, Barney Waria (Gunaia, ['Waria] of Tindale 1937), recorded in Adelaide 1937-1940; Goedemans indexes the language as Tindale T42 'Ngadjuri'. Same languoid as ngad1257 (AIATSIS L5); no dialect distinction is possible.

sources.citation: Berndt, R.M. & T. Vogelsang. 1941. Comparative vocabularies of the Ngadjuri and Dieri tribes, South Australia. Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 65(1): 3-10.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose statement on stress. Only phonetic remark is on the [v]/[bv] sound. All forms are given in Tindale's (1935, 1940) modified-IPA transcription with a stress mark ['] before the stressed syllable; the Ngadjuri forms overwhelmingly carry it word-initially (['vapi] father, ['yadlu] we, ['jaga] sister; rough scanned count ~293 initial-only vs ~57 internal-only marked tokens across the article), with internal marks mostly on compounds/reduplications ([vad'napa] circumcision, [gundi'itji] it, ['mana'tandra]). Single speaker (Barney Waria/Gunaia, aged 77, Adelaide 1940).
